Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help needed

Hi Jasmine / Neha,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and median tail latency from ~13:55 PST in us-west-2. Our storefronts are intermittently failing to generate recommendations; traffic is down ~25% and user complaints are rising. Attached is a small log snippet and a Grafana screenshot (included).

Key points:
- 5xx rate spiked from 0.3% to ~6% between 13:55–14:20 PST
- P95 latency jumped to ~1.6s for generation calls (normal ~220ms)
- No config changes on our side — we only saw an uptick when we started regional pinning to us-west-2

Can you confirm whether this is a regional AZ issue on Redwood or if routing changes happened that might have overloaded the endpoint? This is high customer impact (shopping conversions). We need an exec bridge if this is platform-level.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of IT, CascadeMed

Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help needed

Debug notes (initial):
- Telemetry shows elevated token-queueing and sustained CPU throttling on multiple GPU hosts in us-west-2a starting 13:50 PST.
- Error taxonomy: ~70% internal 502/503 from our local inference mesh (kernel OOM/retry), ~30% from overloaded gateway proxies returning 504.
- No rollout or config push detected from our control plane in the time window.
- Cross-correlation with autoscaler: several nodes entered transient decommission due to a noisy host health signal (we are investigating root cause of noisy health checks).

Mitigation proposal (short horizon):
1) Immediate: enable cross-region steering for CascadeMed traffic to us-east-1 and us-west-1 fallback, with circuit-breaker set to 60s and KV cache warmup. This will reduce load on the degraded AZ while keeping user latency acceptable.
2) Priority capacity: request authorization for temporary dedicated capacity (we can allocate a small reserved pool for ~12–24h) to prevent tail re-amplification.
3) Medium: re-run noisy-host isolation sequence and perform controlled restart of impacted inference pods once load is reduced.

Risks: cross-region steer will increase token latency by ~40–80ms but should eliminate 5xx storm. Need exec sign-off for temporary capacity and to notify broader impacted customers if we change routing policy.

I’m enabling emergency telemetry dashboard and will stand by for the exec bridge.

— Markus Klein
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-steer-plan-v1.pdf

Subject: Cascademed — stabilization update and next steps (post-mitigation)

Julia / Andre — quick update following the exec bridge and mitigation performed yesterday: 

What we did:
- Scoped cross-region steer for CascadeMed traffic to us-east-1 with us-west-1 fallback (scoped only to your account).
- Allocated 24h of temporary priority capacity to prevent re-amplification while we validated host replacements.
- Isolated and rebooted three noisy hosts that triggered repeated decommissions; adjusted host health threshold to avoid false positives while we evaluate root cause.

Result:
- 5xx rate dropped back to baseline (~0.4%) within 22 minutes of the steer activation.
- P95 latency returned to ~240ms (expected ~220ms) after cache warmup.
- No more user-visible failures reported in our telemetry or your dashboard.

Next steps (open):
- Engineering RCA (Markus) — root cause writeup and timeline for permanent mitigation (ETA 48h).
- Customer-facing post-mortem and proposed credit (Jasmine / Sales Ops) — I’ll follow up with proposed credit and timeline for the PM.
- Telemetry share: I’ve uploaded dashboards and logs to the shared Drive link.

We appreciate your patience and flagged this as priority. If you’d like a follow-up call with me and Vanessa to walk through the RCA once ready, I can schedule for early next week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
